110a-box.png: Quantum lab (Gate 14.2): an electron in a 1 nm box — Schrödinger’s equation solved on a 500-point grid; the first four levels agree with Mott’s n²h²/8ml² (0.37603 eV for n = 1). Finding: Mott’s 1-cm example prints 3·2 × 10⁻⁷ V, his formula gives 5.5 × 10⁻⁷ V.
110b-oscillator.png: The harmonic oscillator with ħω = 0.5 eV: numerical levels 0.24999, 0.74997, … against Schrödinger’s (25′) Eₙ = ((2n + 1)/2)hν₀.
110c-tunnel.png: Tunnelling: a 0.5 eV electron through a 1 eV, 0.5 nm barrier passes with T = 0.1014; resonances above the top (Condon & Morse 1929). Finding: their eq. (68.5) is printed with a wrong sign.
111a-binding.png: Nuclei (Gate 14.3): binding energy per nucleon of every NUBASE2020 nuclide; the liquid-drop formula fitted to 2292 of them (rms 2.86 MeV) beside Green’s, Wapstra’s and Bethe & Bacher’s coefficients as tabulated by Wing (1964).
111b-chart.png: The chart of nuclides: every NUBASE2020 ground state with a mass, coloured by half-life.
111c-u238.png: The uranium-238 series (USGS) with NUBASE2020 half-lives: 14 decays from U-238 to stable Pb-206.
111d-pp.png: Fusion in the Sun: NASA’s three steps of the pp chain with energies from NUBASE2020 masses — 1.442, 5.493 and 12.86 MeV, 26.73 MeV in all (PDG: “∼ 26 MeV”).
109a-particles.png: Particles (Gate 14.1): quarks, leptons, gauge bosons and the Higgs with the Particle Data Group’s 2025 values (CC BY 4.0), on a log mass scale from the electron to the top quark; DOE Office of Science sentences.
113a-mercury.png: Tests of relativity (Gate 14.5): Einstein’s 1916 eq. (75) with JPL’s elements gives 42.98″ per century for Mercury — his “43″ pro Jahrhundert” — and smaller advances for the other planets.
113b-light.png: Bending light: eq. (74) gives 1.751″ at the solar limb (printed 1,7″) and falls as 1/Δ.
113c-gpb.png: Gravity Probe B: measured geodetic and frame-dragging drifts against the predictions (Stanford/NASA 2011); Kerr ISCO limits.
114a-rar.png: Dark matter or modified gravity? (Gate 14.6): 2,696 points in 153 SPARC galaxies selected as McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert (2016) did (paper: 2,693); their eq. (4) with g† = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s² and refitted here, 1.16 × 10⁻¹⁰, against Newton’s line.
114b-ngc3198.png: One galaxy: NGC 3198’s observed rotation curve, the Newtonian curve of its stars and gas, and eq. (4) with the paper’s fixed g† — nothing fitted to this galaxy.
112a-plasma.png: Plasma (Gate 14.4): the solar wind near 1 AU (Divine 1973: 5 cm⁻³, 1.5 × 10⁵ K electrons, 5 nT) — plasma frequency 20.1 kHz, Debye length 12 m, Alfvén speed 48.8 km/s from the NRL Plasma Formulary’s formulas; the formulary’s typical plasmas.
